items.title: NEW — `is Some(let x)` on an UNANNOTATED closure parameter binds the payload as `Option`'s own declared parameter `T`, not the instantiation: `outer.sub(\|inner\| if inner is Some(let inner) { inner.len() })` over a `SignalCell<Option<List<i32>>>` is refused "cannot call method 'len' on T" — for EVERY callee shape (std `sub`/`effect`, a non-generic user callee typed `\|Option<i32>\| void`, a user generic `\|Option<T>\|`) and every payload (scalar, `List`, a user struct, a nested `SignalCell`) — while the same `is` on a `let`-bound value is right; and the UNSOUND face: the unbounded `T` reconciles with anything, so `cell.set(inner)` on a `SignalCell<str>` over a `List<i53>` payload COMPILES. Kolt's `channel.vl:199` HACK re-annotates the binding (`let inner: SignalCell<U> = inner`); its guarded `effect` sites compile by this accident
items.discussion: kolt marker sweep 2026-09-10 (the HACK appeared during the session); reproduced on 65af4be0 in thirteen variants (scratchpad `kolt-markers/pa5`); annotating the closure PARAMETER (`\|inner: Option<SignalCell<U>>\|`) is the workaround, so the pattern is typed against the parameter's filled type only when it was written
items.body: The variant pattern's payload is typed when the closure body is walked, against the parameter's UNFILLED type (B185/B227's family): the scrutinee's `Option<..>` is read at the enum's declaration and the payload comes out as the declaration's `T`, a free unbounded generic that later reconciles with anything. Type the pattern against the parameter's filled type (the callee's closure type instantiated by the receiver / the other arguments — the same fill `channels.set(incoming)` already sees for the parameter itself), or defer pattern typing until the fill lands. Pins: the refuse face (`inner.len()` compiles over `Option<List<i32>>`), the unsound face (`SignalCell<str>::set` over a `List<i53>` payload REFUSED), the non-generic callee, and `Ok(let v)` / a user enum for the same shape. Probably one root with B288 (a closure's declared type not fully reconciled) — verify before assigning two lanes.
